subject: Proposal: overage mediation & throttling agreement for Dedicated commit (Orion Health)
messages:
From: Sara Jameson <sara.jameson@orionhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionhealth.com>, procure@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit follow-up / overage handling

Evelyn — thanks for the call this morning. The team liked the baseline commit pricing, but procurement has pushed back hard on unlimited overage exposure. They want a predictable worst-case monthly cap, or at least a clearer throttling and metering approach that preserves availability for our production traffic.

Can you send a concrete proposal that shows:
- what throttling looks like at sustained +50% above commit vs burst +200% for <10 min
- how metering is calculated (per-GPU-minute, per-token, 1-min rolling window?)
- example invoices/credit calculations for a 30% sustained overrun month vs a single-day incident

Thanks — Sara

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jameson <sara.jameson@orionhealth.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit follow-up / overage handling

Sara — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a short proposal and an overage-rate CSV with worked examples. Below is a concise summary tailored to Orion Health so procurement can see options side-by-side.

Key proposals:
1) Tiered overage billing + soft cap option
   - Bursts (<= 10 minutes above commit): no throttling, billed at burst rate (1.5x committed rate) measured using 1-minute windows.
   - Sustained overrun (> 10 minutes continuous above commit): progressive throttling kicks in after a 30-minute sustained window. Billing rate steps down by pre-agreed discount bands, and we offer a monthly soft cap option (up to X% of commit) that converts excess into a discounted add-on instead of pure overage.

2) Metering granularity and lookbacks
   - Primary meter: 1-minute GPU usage windows aggregated per GPU pool.
   - Lookback windows: burst detection uses rolling 10-minute windows; sustained overrun detection uses rolling 30-minute windows with a 24-hour smoothing for reporting.

3) Crediting and mediation path
   - First-time incidents (<= 1 per 12-month period) where customer meets incident postmortem obligations: 25% credit on the overage portion in that month.
   - Repeat sustained overrun: apply throttling policy automatically; credits are evaluated case-by-case when Redwood escalates to the account team.

4) Operational guarantees and SLOs
   - Throughput guarantee: committed capacity will provide >= 95% of committed token throughput in steady-state.
   - During throttling, tail latency SLOs may be relaxed but we commit to priority fallback routes for critical API keys defined in the contract.

Next steps: Marcus (technical lead) proposed a short runbook + telemetry thresholds for SRE -> I suggest a 30-day pilot with the "soft cap" enabled so procurement can evaluate real billing impact.

Evelyn

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jameson <sara.jameson@orionhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit follow-up / overage handling

Sara — quick technical clarification on how throttling would behave:

- Detection: we compute per-pool utilization as (active GPU-seconds / reserved GPU-seconds) sampled each minute. If utilization > 150% for 10 consecutive minutes -> classify as burst; if > 150% for 30 consecutive minutes -> sustained overrun.
- Throttling ladder (configurable per-account):
   * Step 1 (sustained minute 31-60): gentle concurrency reduction (~10% request accept rate decrease) + maintain KV cache prioritization.
   * Step 2 (sustained minute 61-180): stricter queuing, priority windows for pinned API keys, and rate-tiered request shaping.
   * Step 3 (> 180 minutes): switch to capacity-fallback models (quantized lower-cost variant) for non-critical routes; critical routes remain routed to committed capacity until commit exhaustion.
- Billing integration: the system emits an "overage event" for each 10-minute bucket that exceeds commit; billing aggregates these buckets and applies the agreed rate table. We can provide a simulator for Orion to feed historical traces and estimate exposure.

Attached: runbook stub and a sample simulator output for a synthetic 72-hour spike.

Marcus

From: Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jameson <sara.jameson@orionhealth.com>, procure@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit follow-up / overage handling

Thanks — this is useful. A few procurement-specific clarifications before we escalate internally:
1) The soft cap sounds promising. Can you give a concrete example: say we have a 100-GPU commit, 30% sustained overrun for the month — which line items would appear on our invoice and how would the soft cap convert those into a discounted addon?
2) Metering windows — we need to ensure we can reconcile to our own telemetry (we sample at 1s at our side). Can Redwood provide 1-minute aligned meter exports and a reconciliation report?
3) If throttling reduces our effective throughput during a sustained overrun, will Redwood provide temporary capacity credits to account for the reduced throughput?

Appreciate specifics so we can push this through procurement.

Tim

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionhealth.com>, Sara Jameson <sara.jameson@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit follow-up / overage handling

Tim — below are concrete worked examples and answers. I attached the same spreadsheet as a CSV for easy ingestion.

Worked example A (monthly sustained 30% overrun):
- Commit: 100 GPUs equivalent (baseline) billed at committed rate $R per GPU-hour.
- Observed sustained overrun: average 130 GPUs across the month -> excess = 30 GPU-equivalent hours on average.
- Billing path with soft-cap enabled (soft cap = 20% by default):
   * First 20% overrun (i.e., up to 120 GPUs average) is converted to a discounted add-on charged at 0.6x committed rate (invoice line: "Committed soft-add-on: 20% of commit @ 0.6x")
   * Remaining 10% overrun billed as true overage at tiered overage rate (1.2x committed rate) but eligible for the one-time incident credit if customer provides postmortem within 7 days and it's classified as a platform incident.
- Invoice example lines: "Committed baseline: 100 GPUs @ $R", "Soft-add-on (20%): 20 GPUs @ $0.6R", "Overage (10%): 10 GPUs @ $1.2R". Net impact is significantly lower than flat 1.5x overage on full 30%.

Metering and reconciliation:
- We will export per-minute buckets (aligned to UTC minute boundaries) with GPU-second counts and a signature hash for tamper-evident reconciliation.
- Delivery: raw CSV + reconciliation report (diffs flagged >1%), weekly for the invoice month during pilot and monthly thereafter.

Throughput credits during throttling:
- We will provide temporary capacity credits when throttling is applied and measurable throughput loss (>= 10% reduction vs expected committed throughput for >= 4 consecutive hours). Credit calculation: lost GPU-hours * committed rate * 0.5 (50% credit). Credits appear as a line item on the subsequent invoice and do not count against the soft cap.

Proposed commercial path:
- 30-day pilot with soft cap at 20%, metering exports enabled, and a simulator run against Orion's historical traces.
- After pilot: mutual review and adjust soft cap or discount bands.

If this aligns, Marcus and Dev can schedule the simulator run; Karthik can update the MSA redlines to include the soft-cap wording and the incident credit clause.

Evelyn
